title: Graceful-shutdown drain collects channel leftovers into a batch nobody flushes
diff: // Uploader batches telemetry points and ships them to the collector.
// Enqueue never blocks; telemetry is best-effort under backpressure.
+// Run exits when ctx is cancelled. Points accepted by Enqueue before
+// cancellation are delivered: the shutdown path drains whatever is
+// still buffered in the channel before returning.
+// Wait blocks until Run has fully stopped, for use after cancelling
+// the context so main() can exit knowing delivery finished.
+		t.Fatalf("expected a full batch, got %d", client.received())
+		t.Fatalf("expected the buffered point to flush on shutdown, got %d", client.received())

ground_truth.explanation: The ctx.Done() shutdown path flushes first, THEN drains the channel: leftover points are appended to u.batch and the default branch returns as soon as the channel is empty -- without a final flush. Any drained points that do not happen to fill a complete maxBatch are appended and then silently discarded when Run returns, so the method's own comment ('points accepted by Enqueue before cancellation are delivered') is false for up to maxBatch-1 points per shutdown. The flush() call placed before the drain loop makes the path look handled at a glance; the fix is to flush after the drain loop instead (or in both places). TestShutdownFlushesCurrentBatch pins the pre-drain flush behavior (a point already moved into the batch) but no test enqueues points that are still sitting in the channel at cancellation time, which is exactly the drained-then-dropped population.
